findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 changes bold link lightness from 30% to 70% in light themes, making links fainter; preserve 30% for $primary and use 70% for $secondary.
app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 changes .name lightness from 30% to 50% in light themes, removing its color distinction from .title; use the intended 30%/70% pair.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 also changes .name lightness from 30% to 50% in light themes, removing its color distinction from .title; use the intended 30%/70% pair.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 reverses .custom-message-length lightness values to 30% for light themes and 70% for dark themes, making the hint overly prominent and inconsistent with desktop; use 70%/30%.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes h3 lightness from 20% to 50% in light themes, giving it the same color as h4 and weakening heading hierarchy; preserve the desktop equivalent's 20%/80% pair.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 reverses .custom-message-length lightness values to 30% for light themes and 70% for dark themes, making the hint overly prominent and inconsistent with desktop; use 70%/30%.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 102 of mobile/modal.scss: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. The dark-light-choose function takes (light-theme-value, dark-theme-value). Using 30% lightness on $primary for light themes makes the text darker/more prominent, while 70% lightness on $secondary for dark themes also makes it more prominent. Looking at the desktop version in desktop/modal.scss line 91, it uses `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` which is the opposite - 70% for light themes (lighter/less prominent) and 30% for dark themes. This is indeed an inconsistency where mobile reverses the values compared to desktop, making the hint text more prominent on mobile when it should be subtle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes h3 lightness from 20% to 50% in light themes, giving it the same color as h4 and weakening heading hierarchy; preserve the desktop equivalent's 20%/80% pair.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at mobile/topic-post.scss line 182 shows the h3 color changing from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light theme value from 20% to 50% lightness, which is the same as h4's value (line 187 shows h4 uses 50%/50%). The desktop equivalent at desktop/topic-post.scss line 321 uses 20%/80% for h3, maintaining distinction from h4. This is a legitimate visual hierarchy bug where h3 and h4 would have identical colors in light themes.
